newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SKIPPER JOHNSON SITS OUT SECOND LIONS GAME.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SKIPPER JOHNSON SITS OUT SECOND LIONS GAME.

text.p: British Lions skipper Martin Johnson was again left on the sidelines when the side was announced on Monday for the second match of the South African tour.
Scotland skipper Rob Wainwright will lead the side against Border in East London on Wednesday with Johnson being rested until Saturday's clash with Western Province in Cape Town.
"Martin's chomping at the bit to play but it was a management decision taken with him to make sure he was fresh and rested to play in the big games," said team manager Fran Cotton.
"He has had a lot of rugby right up until the end of the season and we thought he needed three good weeks to get fit and fresh and raring to go."
Lock Doddie Weir plays his second match of the week in place of Johnson as the Lions' selectors give first starting appearances of the tour to 14 other players.
Welsh centre Scott Gibbs, who played two tests for the Lions in New Zealand in 1993, is one of four former rugby league players in the line-up.
He is reunited with Welsh international centre partner Alan Bateman while David Young, also of Wales, is in the front row and the fourth returnee from league, John Bentley, plays on the wing.
"We made a good start on Saturday and we aim to continue that," said Wainwright reflecting on Saturday's opening 39-11 victory over an Eastern Province XV.

"It's important to note that we have a lot of sub-units in the team with the back three from Newcastle, the centres from Wales and Neil Back and Eric Millar who work well together for Leicester in the back row. This is a new team and they will hopefully give us some cohesion."
The announcement was made after an intense morning training session which saw hookers Mark Regan of England and Barry Williams of Wales twice erupt in a flurry of punches during scrummaging practice.
"It was a pretty intense session all-round, pretty ferocious at times and there's a lot of personal pride at stake and occasionally you get the odd little flare-up," explained Cotton.
"But it remains on the training field -- it's nothing serious, we've seen it many times before."

Wainwright added: "Live scrummaging practice is always difficult and there was a clash of heads which led to a flare-up but the two main protagonists have had a chat and laugh about it and it's all over."

Scottish prop Tom Smith sat out training because of a continuing problem with a neck spasm while Tim Rodber required five stitches in a cut above his right eye. He is expected to play on Saturday along with Johnson, Alan Tait, Matt Dawson, Barry Willims and Paul Wallace -- the six players yet to start a match.

Border - 15-Russell Bennett (captain); 14-Kelly Hilton-Green, 13-Greg Hechter, 12-Kaya Malotana, 11-Andre Claasen; 10-Greg Miller, 9-John Bradbrook; 8-Andre Fox, 7-Anton Botha, 6-Marius Swart, 5-Johan Gehring, 4-Streicher Botha, 3-Delarey du Preez, 2-uhan van Zyl, 1-Heinrich Kok.

British Lions - 15-Tim Stimpson; 14-John Bentley, 13-Scott Gibbs, 12-Alan Bateman, 11-Tony Underwood; 10-Paul Grayson, 9-Austin Healey; 8-Eric Millar, 7-Neil Back, 6-Rob Wainwright (captain), 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Doddie Weir, 3-David Young, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.
